metadata.title: Problems and Results on 3-Chromatic Hypergraphs and Some Related Questions
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.
metadata.venue: Colloquia Mathematica Societatis Janos Bolyai 10, Infinite and Finite Sets, Keszthely (Hungary), 1973

nodes.name: Hypergraph (basic terminology)
nodes.statement: A hypergraph is a collection of sets; this paper deals only with finite hypergraphs. The sets are called edges, their elements are points. The degree of a point is the number of edges containing it. A hypergraph is $r$-uniform if every edge has $r$ points.

nodes.name: Simple hypergraph and clique
nodes.statement: A hypergraph is simple if any two edges have at most one common point. It is called a clique if any two edges have at least one common point.

nodes.name: Chromatic number of a hypergraph
nodes.statement: The chromatic number of a hypergraph is the least number $k$ such that the points can be $k$-colored so that no edge is monochromatic.

nodes.name: Property B (Miller)
nodes.statement: Property B (introduced by Miller for infinite edges) is the property of having chromatic number $2$, i.e. the points admit a $2$-coloring leaving no edge monochromatic.
nodes.origin_citation: Miller (cited as introducing 'property B' for infinite edges)

nodes.name: $m_k(r)$ and $m_k^*(r)$, $n_k^*(r)$
nodes.statement: $m_k(r)$ is the minimum number of edges in a $(k+1)$-chromatic $r$-uniform hypergraph. $n_k^*(r)$ and $m_k^*(r)$ denote the minimum number of points and edges in a $(k+1)$-chromatic $r$-uniform simple hypergraph.

nodes.name: Line-graph of a hypergraph
nodes.statement: Given $H$ with edges $E_1, \ldots, E_m$, its line-graph has vertices $v_1, \ldots, v_m$ where $v_i$ is adjacent to $v_j$ iff $E_i \cap E_j \neq \emptyset$.

nodes.name: Circuit (in a hypergraph)
nodes.statement: Used implicitly in Theorem 1': a hypergraph contains no circuit of length $<s$ if it has girth at least $s$ in the standard hypergraph sense.
nodes.notes: The paper invokes 'circuits of length $<s$' without an explicit local definition; it follows the standard hypergraph girth notion used in [4].

nodes.name: $m^{**}(r)$, $M(r)$, $N(r)$ for cliques
nodes.statement: $m^{**}(r)$ is the minimum number of edges in a $3$-chromatic $r$-uniform clique. $M(r)$ is the maximum number of edges in such a clique. $N(r)$ is the maximum number of points in a $3$-chromatic $r$-uniform clique.

nodes.name: $q(r)$
nodes.statement: $q(r)$ is the smallest integer for which there exists an $r$-uniform clique on $q(r)$ edges that cannot be covered by fewer than $r$ points.

nodes.name: $\Delta(H) = \{|E \cap F| : E,F \in H, E \neq F\}$
nodes.statement: For a hypergraph $H$, $\Delta(H) = \{|E \cap F| : E, F \in H, E \neq F\}$ is the set of pairwise edge-intersection sizes.

nodes.name: Trivial observation linking chromatic number to common-point structure
nodes.statement: If a hypergraph has chromatic number $\geq 3$ then it has two edges with exactly one common point.

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (asymptotic order of $n_k^*$ and $m_k^*$)
nodes.statement: $\lim_{r \to \infty} \frac{1}{r}\sqrt[r]{n_k^*(r)} = k$ and $\lim_{r \to \infty} \sqrt[r]{m_k^*(r)} = k^2$.
nodes.notes: OCR garbled some symbols; reconstructed from context. In particular this implies $c_1 \frac{4^r}{r} < m_2^*(r) < c_2 r^4 \cdot 4^r$, so $m_2^*(r) \gg m_2(r)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1' (probabilistic existence of high-girth high-chromatic uniform hypergraphs)
nodes.statement: Let $s \geq 2$, $r \geq 2$, $k \geq 2$, $n = 4 \cdot 20^{s-1} r^{3s-2}(k-1)^{s(r+1)}$, $m = 4 \cdot 20^s r^{3s-2} k^{s(r+1)}$, $d = 20 r^2 k^{r-1}$. There exists an $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ on $kn$ points with at most $m$ edges, all degrees $\leq d$, no circuits of length $<s$, and such that every set of $n$ points contains an edge.
conclusions: there exists an $r$-uniform $H$ on $k\cdot n$ points, with $\leq m$ edges, max degree $\leq d$, girth $\geq s$, every $n$-subset contains an edge
nodes.notes: Yields the upper bounds in Theorem 1. Some exponents may be slightly garbled by OCR.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1' (greedy / probabilistic edge-by-edge construction)
nodes.statement: Construct $H = \{E_1, \ldots, E_t\}$ inductively: at stage $p$, pick $E_{p+1}$ contained in as many of the still-uncovered $n$-element sets $S_1, \ldots, S_{x_p}$ as possible, while preserving the no-short-circuit and bounded-degree constraints. Show $x_{p+1} \leq x_p(1 - 20 k^r/n)$, hence the procedure terminates in $<m$ steps.

nodes.name: Inductive setup: bookkeep uncovered $n$-sets
nodes.statement: Suppose $E_1, \ldots, E_p$ have been chosen satisfying ($\alpha$) no short circuits and ($\beta$) every point in at most $d$ edges. Let $S_1, \ldots, S_{x_p}$ be the $n$-sets containing none of these edges; if $x_p = 0$ we are done.

nodes.name: Count low-degree points in each $S_j$
nodes.statement: Let $N$ be the number of points of $S_j$ of degree $d$; then $d N' \leq r p \leq r m$, so $N \leq r m / d$. Hence $S_j$ has at least $n(1 - r m/(d n))$ points of degree $<d$.

nodes.name: Bound $r$-tuples excluded by the girth condition
nodes.statement: Each existing edge $E_i$ contributes at most $\binom{r^{s'} d^{s'-1}}{2} \leq r^{2s'} d^{2s'-2}$ pairs whose use would create a short circuit, for $s = 2s'$. So the number of forbidden pairs is $\leq m\, r^{2s'} d^{2s'-2}$.

nodes.name: Show many $r$-tuples remain, derive recursion
nodes.statement: Subtracting forbidden $r$-tuples from $\binom{n}{r}$ leaves $\geq \binom{n}{r}/2$. Counting incidences gives some $r$-tuple of $S$ valid for $\geq x_p \cdot 20 k^r / n$ of the $S_j$. Choosing it as $E_{p+1}$ yields $x_{p+1} \leq x_p(1 - 20 k^r / n)$.

nodes.name: Termination bound
nodes.statement: Iterating the recursion, $x_m \leq x_0 (1 - 20 k^r/n)^m \leq \binom{kn}{n} e^{-20 m k^r/n} = 1$. Hence the procedure halts before step $m$, giving the required $H$ with $\leq m$ edges.

nodes.name: Theorem 2 (high-degree edge in chromatic-rich uniform hypergraphs)
nodes.statement: A $(k+1)$-chromatic $r$-uniform hypergraph contains an edge intersected by at least $k^{r-1}/4$ other edges. Consequently, the valency of at least one vertex is $\geq k^{r-1}/(4r)$.
conclusions: some edge of $H$ is intersected by $\geq k^{r-1}/4$ other edges

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2 via the local lemma
nodes.statement: Color each point of $H$ uniformly at random with $k$ colors. Let $A_i$ be the event '$E_i$ is monochromatic'; $P(A_i) = k/k^r = 1/k^{r-1}$. The line-graph has max degree $d \leq k^{r-1}/4$, so $P(A_i) \leq 1/(4d)$ and the lemma yields $P(\overline{A_1} \cdots \overline{A_m}) > 0$, i.e. a proper $k$-coloring exists.

nodes.name: Lovasz Local Lemma (symmetric form)
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $d$ and vertices $v_1, \ldots, v_n$. Associate event $A_i$ with $v_i$ and assume $A_i$ is independent of $\{A_j : (v_i, v_j) \notin E(G)\}$, and $P(A_i) \leq 1/(4d)$. Then $P(\overline{A_1} \cdots \overline{A_n}) > 0$.
assumptions: for each $i$, $A_i$ independent of $\{A_j : (v_i, v_j) \notin E(G)\}$
nodes.notes: This is the famous symmetric Lovasz Local Lemma, introduced in this paper. The OCR shows the bound $P(A_i) \leq 1/(4d)$; the constant $4$ is the original constant (later improvements give $e \cdot d \cdot p \leq 1$).

nodes.name: Proof of the Local Lemma (induction on $n$)
nodes.statement: Prove the stronger statement $P(A_1 \mid \overline{A_2} \cdots \overline{A_n}) \leq 1/(2d)$ by induction on $n$. For $n=1$ trivial; for $n \geq 2$ split conditional probabilities over neighbors of $v_1$ in $G$ and use the inductive hypothesis.

nodes.name: Strengthened induction hypothesis
nodes.statement: Prove $P(A_1 \mid \overline{A_2} \cdots \overline{A_n}) \leq 1/(2d)$. This implies the conclusion since $P(\overline{A_1} \cdots \overline{A_n}) = \prod_i P(\overline{A_i} \mid \overline{A_{i+1}} \cdots \overline{A_n}) > 0$.

nodes.name: Split into neighbors and non-neighbors of $v_1$
nodes.statement: Let $v_2, \ldots, v_q$ be neighbors of $v_1$ in $G$ ($q \leq d+1$). Write $P(A_1 \mid \overline{A_2} \cdots \overline{A_n}) = P(A_1 \overline{A_2} \cdots \overline{A_q} \mid \overline{A_{q+1}} \cdots \overline{A_n}) / P(\overline{A_2} \cdots \overline{A_q} \mid \overline{A_{q+1}} \cdots \overline{A_n})$.

nodes.name: Bound numerator by independence
nodes.statement: By the independence assumption, $P(A_1 \overline{A_2} \cdots \overline{A_q} \mid \overline{A_{q+1}} \cdots \overline{A_n}) \leq P(A_1 \mid \overline{A_{q+1}} \cdots \overline{A_n}) = P(A_1) \leq 1/(4d)$.

nodes.name: Bound denominator via inductive hypothesis
nodes.statement: $P(\overline{A_2} \cdots \overline{A_q} \mid \overline{A_{q+1}} \cdots \overline{A_n}) \geq 1 - \sum_{i=2}^{q} P(A_i \mid \overline{A_{q+1}} \cdots \overline{A_n}) \geq 1 - (q-1)/(2d) \geq 1/2$.

nodes.name: Combine to conclude
nodes.statement: Combining: $P(A_1 \mid \overline{A_2} \cdots \overline{A_n}) \leq (1/(4d)) / (1/2) = 1/(2d)$, completing the induction.

nodes.name: Corollary 1 to Theorem 2 (degree-based colorability)
nodes.statement: If each point of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ has degree $\leq k^{r-1}/(4r)$ then the chromatic number of $H$ is $\leq k$.

nodes.name: Corollary 2 to Theorem 2 (vertex lower bound for simple chromatic-rich)
nodes.statement: If $H$ is a simple $(k+1)$-chromatic $r$-uniform hypergraph then $|V(H)| \geq c \cdot k^{r-1}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3 (rainbow coloring under bounded edge intersection)
nodes.statement: If each edge of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ meets at most $k^{r-1}/(4(k-1)^r)$ other edges, then the vertices of $H$ can be $k$-colored so that each color meets each edge.
assumptions: each edge of $H$ meets $\leq k^{r-1}/(4(k-1)^r)$ other edges
conclusions: $H$ admits a $k$-coloring such that each color appears in every edge

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3
nodes.statement: Color the points uniformly at random with $k$ colors. Let $A_i$ be the event '$E_i$ does not get all $k$ colors'; then $P(A_i) \leq k(1 - 1/k)^r$. The line-graph has $d \leq k^{r-1}/(4(k-1)^r)$, so $P(A_i) \leq 1/(4d)$ and the local lemma applies.

nodes.name: Theorem 4 (strong Strauss conjecture for lattice points)
nodes.statement: Let $\epsilon > 0$, $k \geq 2$, $n \geq 1$. There is $r_0 = r_0(k, \epsilon)$ such that if $S$ is a set of lattice points in $\mathbb{Z}^n$ with $|S| = r > r_0$, then the lattice points can be $k$-colored so that every translate $S + a$ contains at least $(1-\epsilon)r/k$ points of any given color.
conclusions: the lattice points admit a $k$-coloring such that each translate $S+a$ has $\geq (1-\epsilon)r/k$ points of every color

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4 (compactness + local lemma)
nodes.statement: By compactness, suffices for finite $H$ of translates. Random $k$-color the vertices: each translate has $<(1-\epsilon)r/k$ of one color with probability $(1-\delta)^r$ where $\delta = \delta(k,\epsilon)$ from CLT. Each translate meets $<r^2$ others, so $(1-\delta)^r < 1/(4 r^2)$ for $r$ large; the local lemma applies.

nodes.name: Theorem 5 (many high-degree vertices in simple chromatic-rich)
nodes.statement: If $H$ is a simple $(k+1)$-chromatic $r$-uniform hypergraph then it contains at least $k^{r-2}/(4(r-1))$ points of degree $\geq k^{r-2}/(4(r-1))$.
conclusions: $H$ has $\geq k^{r-2}/(4(r-1))$ vertices of degree $\geq k^{r-2}/(4(r-1))$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5 (delete-and-apply-Theorem 2)
nodes.statement: For each edge $E$, let $t(E) \in E$ be a max-degree vertex; set $E' = E \setminus \{t(E)\}$, $H' = \{E' : E \in H\}$. Then $H'$ is not $k$-colorable (any $k$-coloring lifts to one of $H$), so by Theorem 2 has a vertex $x$ of degree $\geq k^{r-2}/(4(r-1))$. The corresponding $t(E_i)$'s have the desired degrees.

nodes.name: Corollary 1 to Theorem 5 (covering lower bound for simple chromatic-rich)
nodes.statement: A $(k+1)$-chromatic $r$-uniform simple hypergraph cannot be covered by less than $k^{r-2}/(4(r-1))$ points.

nodes.name: Corollary 2 to Theorem 5 (matching size lower bound)
nodes.statement: A $(k+1)$-chromatic $r$-uniform simple hypergraph contains at least $k^{r-2}/(4r(r-1))$ pairwise disjoint edges.

nodes.name: Corollary 3 to Theorem 5 (edge lower bound for simple chromatic-rich)
nodes.statement: A $(k+1)$-chromatic $r$-uniform simple hypergraph has at least $k^{2(r-2)}/(16 r(r-1)^2)$ edges.

nodes.name: Construction (a): all $r$-subsets of $2r-1$ points
nodes.statement: All $r$-tuples from a set of $2r-1$ points form a $3$-chromatic $r$-uniform clique.

nodes.name: Construction (b): partition-extension construction
nodes.statement: Let $|S| = 2r-2$. For each partition $P = \{S_1, S_2\}$ with $|S_1| = |S_2| = r-1$ adjoin a new point $x_P$. Take $H$ to consist of all $r$-tuples from $S$ together with all $r$-tuples $S_1 \cup \{x_P\}$. Then $H$ is a $3$-chromatic $r$-uniform clique.

nodes.name: Construction (c): adjoin a $T$ of size $r+1$
nodes.statement: If $H$ is a $3$-chromatic $r$-uniform clique and $T$ is disjoint from $V(H)$ with $|T| = r+1$, define $H'$ to consist of $T$ and all $(r+1)$-tuples $E \cup \{t\}$ for $E \in H, t \in T$. Then $H'$ is an $(r+1)$-uniform $3$-chromatic clique.

nodes.name: Construction (d): blow-up via $H_1, \ldots, H_n$
nodes.statement: Let $H$ be a $3$-chromatic $r$-uniform clique on $V(H) = \{1, \ldots, n\}$ and $H_1, \ldots, H_n$ be $3$-chromatic $p$-uniform cliques on disjoint vertex sets. Then $H^* = \{E_{i_1} \cup \cdots \cup E_{i_r} : E_{i_j} \in H_{i_j}, \{i_1, \ldots, i_r\} \in H\}$ is a $(pr)$-uniform $3$-chromatic clique.

nodes.name: Theorem 6 (small $3$-chromatic cliques)
nodes.statement: $m^{**}(r) \leq 7^{(r-1)/2}$ (or $7^{(3^k-1)/2}$ for $r = 3^k$) for infinitely many $r$.
nodes.notes: Bound exponent partially garbled by OCR; the construction starts with the Fano plane and iterates Construction (d).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6 (iterated Fano construction)
nodes.statement: Apply (d) inductively with $H^{(1)}$ the Fano plane (7 lines on 7 points), $H = H^{(k)}$, and the inner cliques all Fano planes to obtain $H^{(k+1)}$ which is $3^k$-uniform with $|H^{(k+1)}| = 7^{3^k} \cdot |H^{(k)}|$. So $|H^{(k)}| = 7^{1 + 3 + \cdots + 3^{k-1}} = 7^{(3^k-1)/2}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 7 (bounds on $M(r)$, max edges in $3$-chromatic $r$-uniform clique)
nodes.statement: $r! (e - 1) \leq M(r) \leq r^r$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7
nodes.statement: Lower bound: starting with the triangle, repeatedly apply (c) to obtain $r$-uniform $3$-chromatic cliques with $(e-1) r!$ edges. Upper bound: in any $r$-uniform clique with $>r^r$ edges, build $x_1, \ldots, x_r$ with $>r^{r-i}$ edges containing $x_1, \ldots, x_i$; eventually two edges share $r$ points, contradiction. (Uses only that $H$ cannot be covered by $<r$ points.)

nodes.name: Theorem 8 (bounds on $N(r)$, max points in $3$-chromatic $r$-uniform clique)
nodes.statement: $\binom{2r-2}{r-1} \cdot 2 \leq N(r) \leq \frac{1}{2}\binom{2r-1}{r-1}^{-1} \cdot r!$ (bounds approximate due to OCR; the upper bound follows from a Lubell-style permutation count).
nodes.notes: Exact constants obscured in OCR; the upper bound is proved via a sharpening of Calczynska-Karlowicz [1] using Lubell's method [2].

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 8 (Lubell-style permutation argument)
nodes.statement: Lower bound: construction (b). Upper bound (auxiliary lemma): if $H$ is an $r$-uniform clique such that for every vertex $x$ there are edges $E,F$ with $E \cap F = \{x\}$, then $|V(H)| \leq \binom{2r-1}{r-1} \cdot r! / (2(r-1)!^2)$ (count permutations $(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ where $\{x_1,\ldots,x_j\}$ and $\{x_j,\ldots,x_n\}$ both contain edges).

nodes.name: Lemma (Lubell-style sharpening of Calczynska-Karlowicz)
nodes.statement: If $H$ is an $r$-uniform clique such that for each point $x$ there are two edges $E, F$ with $E \cap F = \{x\}$, then $|V(H)| \leq \binom{2r-1}{r-1} r! / (2[(r-1)!]^2 \cdot \binom{2r-1}{r-1})$ (approx: $|V(H)| = O(\binom{2r-1}{r-1})$).
assumptions: for each vertex $x \in V(H)$, there exist edges $E, F$ with $E \cap F = \{x\}$
conclusions: $|V(H)|$ is bounded by an explicit binomial-coefficient expression as in the proof of Theorem 8

nodes.name: Erdos-Lovasz-Shelah common-intersection bound
nodes.statement: If $H$ is a $3$-chromatic $r$-uniform clique then there are two edges $E, F \in H$ with $|E \cap F| \geq r/\log r$.
nodes.notes: Attributed in the paper to Shelah and the authors.

nodes.name: Theorem 9 ($|\Delta(H)| \geq 3$ for large $r$)
nodes.statement: If $r$ is large enough and $H$ is an $r$-uniform $3$-chromatic clique, then the cardinalities $|E \cap F|$ for $E, F \in H$ take at least $3$ distinct values.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 9 (uses a theorem of Deza)
nodes.statement: Suppose $|\Delta(H)| \leq 2$. We know $1 \in \Delta(H)$. Since $|H| \geq 2^{r-1}$, two points $x, y$ lie in $\geq 2^{r-1}/r^2$ edges $F_1, \ldots, F_t$. Any two have at least $2$ common points, so $\Delta(H) = \{1, k\}$. As $t > r^2 - r + 1$ for $r$ large, Deza's theorem [8] forces $F_i \cap F_j = M$ constant; an uncovered edge then has $>r$ points, contradiction.

nodes.name: Theorem 10 (bounds on $q(r)$)
nodes.statement: $\frac{8}{3} r - 3 < q(r) < c \cdot r^{3} \log r$ (constants partially obscured by OCR; the upper bound is roughly $c r^{5/2} \log r$ via a finite-projective-plane construction).
assumptions: $r$ large enough; in part II, $r = p^a + 1$ for prime power $p$
nodes.notes: OCR garbles the precise upper bound exponent; the proof uses $t = 4 r^{3/2} \log r$ random lines in a finite plane of order $r-1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 10 (greedy lower bound + random projective lines upper bound)
nodes.statement: Lower bound: greedily pick max-degree points $x_1, x_2, \ldots$; each removes many edges, so $\leq (8/3)r - 3$ edges suffice to be covered by $r-1$ points. Upper bound: in a finite projective plane of order $r-1$, choose $t = 4 r^{3/2} \log r$ lines uniformly; show that the fraction of choices coverable by $r-1$ points tends to $0$.

nodes.name: Lower-bound greedy peeling
nodes.statement: Iteratively remove a max-degree point $x_{i+1}$ from $H - x_1 - \cdots - x_i$. The degree drop is $\geq 4, 3, 2$ at the corresponding edge-count thresholds, so $(8/3)r - 3$ initial edges shrink to $\leq r+1$ after enough rounds, then to $\leq r-1$ points cover.

nodes.name: Setup of finite-plane random construction
nodes.statement: Let $r = p^a + 1$, edges = lines of a projective plane of order $r-1$. Choose $t = 4 r^{3/2} \log r$ lines uniformly from $r^2 - r + 1$ lines. Show that almost no such choice can be covered by $r-1$ points.

nodes.name: Auxiliary lemma on $B$ (lines disjoint from $\{v_1,\ldots,v_k\}$)
nodes.statement: Using $\sum_i \binom{e_i}{2} = \binom{r-1}{2}$ (eq. (12)) and $B = \sum (e_i - 1) + 1$, derive: $B \geq (r - \sqrt{r})(r - r/\sqrt{r})$ if $e_1 \leq r - C$, else $B \geq r-1$.

nodes.name: Probability bounds in two regimes ($e_1 > r - \sqrt{r}$ and $e_1 \leq r - \sqrt{r}$)
nodes.statement: Estimate the proportion of $t$-line choices coverable by $r-1$ points in each regime; both proportions are $o(1)$.

nodes.name: Conclude existence of an uncoverable family
nodes.statement: Combining the two regimes, almost all choices of $t = 4 r^{3/2} \log r$ lines cannot be covered by $r-1$ points; hence $q(r) \leq c r^{3/2} \cdot O(\log r)$.

nodes.name: Bound (1) (Lovasz-Woodall criterion for $2$-chromaticity)
nodes.statement: For all $H' \subseteq H$: $|\bigcup_{E \in H'} E| \geq |H'| + 1 \;\Rightarrow\; H$ is $2$-chromatic.

nodes.name: Conjecture: $f(r) \to \infty$ for nonuniform $3$-chromatic hypergraphs
nodes.statement: Let $f(r) = \min \sum_{k=1}^{m} 2^{-|E_k|}$ over $3$-chromatic hypergraphs with $\min |E_k| = r$. Then $f(r) \to \infty$ as $r \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Conjecture: weakened (1) for simple hypergraphs
nodes.statement: For simple hypergraphs, the Lovasz-Woodall condition (1) can perhaps be weakened to $|\bigcup_{E \in H'} E| \geq |H'|^{1/2}(1+\epsilon)$ for all $H' \subseteq H$, still implying $2$-chromaticity.

nodes.name: Open problem: is $\lim m^{**}(r)^{1/r} > 2$?
nodes.statement: Is $\lim_{r \to \infty} m^{**}(r)^{1/r}$ greater than $2$? We cannot even show $m^{**}(r) > m_2(r)$.

nodes.name: Open problem: $\max \Delta(H) \geq r - O(1)$ for $3$-chromatic $r$-uniform cliques?
nodes.statement: Can the bound $\max \Delta(H) \geq r/\log r$ be replaced by $c \cdot r$ or even $r - c$? The worst known example has $|E \cap F| \leq r - 2$; no example with $|E \cap F| < r - 3$ is known.

nodes.name: Open problem: $|\Delta(H)| \to \infty$?
nodes.statement: Does $|\Delta(H)| \to \infty$ as $r \to \infty$ for $r$-uniform $3$-chromatic cliques? Best known: $|\Delta(H)| \geq 3$ for large $r$ (Theorem 9).

nodes.name: Open problem: $q(r) \leq c \cdot r$?
nodes.statement: It is challenging to prove or disprove $q(r) \leq c \cdot r$. The authors believe $q(r) \leq c r \log r$ holds.

nodes.name: Strauss problem (existence of $f(k)$ for translate-coloring)
nodes.statement: Is there a function $f(k)$ such that if $S \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ has $|S| = f(k)$, then the integers can be $k$-colored so that each color meets every translated copy $S + a$ of $S$?

nodes.name: Remark added in proof: J. Beck improvement
nodes.statement: J. Beck (Budapest) recently proved $m_2(r)/2^r \to \infty$ (oral communication).

nodes.name: Deza's sunflower theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: If a family of $r$-element sets has more than $r^2 - r + 1$ members and pairwise intersections of constant size, then all pairwise intersections coincide ($F_i \cap F_j = M$ constant for all $i, j$).

nodes.name: Lovasz-Woodall theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: In every $3$-chromatic $r$-uniform hypergraph there is a vertex of degree $> r$. Equivalently: condition (1) implies $2$-chromaticity.

nodes.name: Calczynska-Karlowicz theorem (cited; sharpened by Lemma in Sec. 3)
nodes.statement: A theorem on families of finite sets relating cardinality of vertex set to clique structure; sharpened in this paper via Lubell's method.
